/api/v1/auth/refresh` takes `{ refreshToken }` in the body (it has no cookie to read it
from) and returns a fresh pair; the previous refresh token's SHA-256 hash on the user row is
checked (constant-time) and replaced with a compare-and-swap (`updateMany` filtered by the
hash just verified), so a stolen-and-replayed old token is rejected once it's been rotated
and two concurrent refreshes with the same token can't both win. Never bcrypt for this hash:
bcrypt only reads 72 bytes, and that prefix of a JWT is the same for every token of the same
user — bcrypt stays for passwords only. Every refresh token carries a random `jti`, so two
signed in the same second are still different.
